original_card.question: Can a template or call contract leave two or more unpaid coordinates per live family?
methods: State a replacement for the coverage identity (mass = 72W + 64N) and the contract change that realizes it, with its implementation cost.
Find an obstruction: show which data-endpoint obligation forces exactly one unpaid coordinate in the current template.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An explicit replacement identity, verified on a small complete instance with dirty inputs, priced with ceiling.ceiling(unpaid=...). A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Explain where the single unpaid coordinate per family comes from in the hosted template; propose one change and price it. Ideal budget: two unpaid coordinates per family is 3.77x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The deficit is one coordinate per family minus the centre charge; doubling unpaid coordinates per family scales it directly.
allowed_variations: One template change or one endpoint-contract change.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Counting a coordinate as unpaid while leaving it unadvanced in the data endpoint.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Scalar decoders c*I_112 = A diag(c_t) B^T (any field, any denominators) on the exact PR2297 five-frame cover with the full-port tariff: is every decoder above the zero-saving bound C <= 492 for the u=5 coverage lever row?
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a coverage-law change in general. This package answers the single open residual of the k-port (u=5) lever row on the PR2297 cover: the unmatched-span, even-denominator scalar decoders left open by PR #2879 (equal spans) and philippeVV Theorem 1 / PR #2532 (2-integral). Deciding it settles whether that lever row can save anything.
bottleneck_link: The coverage-law card asks for contracts with more unpaid coordinates per family. The k-port scalar decoder row (u=5, the k=5 port-group route) was a candidate on the PR2297 cover. Proving C >= 554 for every scalar decoder (budget 4432/9, deficit = budget minus cost <= -554/9) closes that row for scalar decoders: a saving there needs something other than a different scalar decoder (a mask with free pairs, another tariff, another cover, or another endpoint contract such as an operator- or block-valued decoder, e.g. PR2297's C_E^2 blocks or PR #3480).
stop_rule: Hard gate 2026-10-19T00:35Z: either a complete checkable proof route or an explicit exact decoder with C <= 492, otherwise no PR. Gate passed at 00:25Z with an exact dual certificate; no large searches; stdlib verifier under 50 MB.
evidence: PROOF.md: principal-rank count (Lemma 1, rank over the base field, no 2-adic step) plus LP duality over the 107 flats (Lemma 2). CERTIFICATE.json: 88 group sets, integer weights over 10^6, all 11449 ordered flat-pair constraints checked exactly (min slack 6/10^6), value 553996479/1000000 > 553, so C >= 554 by integrality; the direct decoder attains 554. verify.py (stdlib, ~2 s) also enumerates flats and pairing ranks by two methods each, checks 2000 random non-closed supports, an exact rational decoder instance (cost 691) and six negative controls (including a mutated cover with a free group pair, rejected by the premise check). PASS_PR2297_PRINCIPAL_RANK_FLOOR.
author: Sagar Thakrar (thakrarsagar)
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance from Claude (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5) in the proof idea, LP search, verifier, certificate and writing, within one automated research loop session. Reviewed in two rounds of independent AI review passes in the same loop (reproducibility, mathematics, provenance, referee); two of those passes recomputed the certificate with separate scripts; no human review.

open_questions.question: Does the clique-restricted principal-rank LP (group sets with no orthogonal pair) reach 297, or 299, on the PR2041 triad cover?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR #2879's 297 is an equal-span floor only, so the unmatched-span class on the literal PR2041 cover is still open; a clique LP value >= 297 closes it. A value >= 299 also excludes the uniform-three completion (budget 896/3 = 298.67), provided the certificate's sets avoid the completed group and the tariff is monotone under the completion.
open_questions.first_step: Check the rank-57 triad line first (PR #2757 and PR #3684 by flyingviper; PR #3505, #3513, #3527 and #3538 by Nick Petalas). Then run the find_certificate.py LP with candidate sets restricted to orthogonal-pair-free group sets of the PR2041 cover, and certify exactly.

open_questions.question: Is there a principal-rank analogue for masks with free pairs (cliques of the nonorthogonality graph only) that is not also valid for line ports?
open_questions.why_it_matters: philippeVV's follow-up 4 shows line-valid bounds cap at 128 on plane covers, so a useful bound must be plane-specific.
open_questions.first_step: Check the concurrent lost-free plane-mask line first (open PRs #3625 by Matarener, #3674 by ToikY, #3676 and #3756 by James Reed). Then compute the clique-restricted LP on philippeVV's a23 plane assignment and compare with 128.
open_questions.blocked_by: needs the a23 plane assignment from philippeVV/integer-mult-bounds@5c81aa40 pinned in this repository

open_questions.question: Which k-port change (a mask with free pairs, another tariff, another cover, or a non-scalar endpoint contract) still has room for a coverage saving now that the PR2297 u=5 scalar row is closed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It identifies which routes remain for the k-port lever row; the scalar-decoder route on this cover is closed.
open_questions.first_step: For a proposed k-port contract, state which of the four it changes before pricing a decoder; for operator- or block-valued decoders (PR2297's C_E^2 blocks, PR #3480 by Gonzalo Mier) state their complete identity and charges.
